figures.alt: Photo of a beaver swimming beside its lodge of sticks in a calm pond with cattails.
figures.caption: A beaver builds a home from sticks. It changes its place to meet its needs.

figures.alt: Photo of a brown deer drinking at a forest stream surrounded by ferns and trees.
figures.caption: A deer needs water, food, air and space. A forest stream gives it water.

figures.alt: Photo of a sand dune on Lake Michigan with beach grass and a gull flying over the blue lake.
figures.caption: A sand dune is a different habitat. Beach grass and gulls live here, not the same living things as a forest.

figures.alt: Illustration of three people planting native wildflowers in a raised garden bed with trowels, one of them using a wheelchair, with bees nearby.
figures.caption: A real action that helps a habitat: planting native flowers for pollinators.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Kinds of living things in each habitat. Pond 4 kinds, Forest 6 kinds, Sand dune 3 kinds.
figures.caption: Picture counts: the pond had 4 kinds of living things, the forest 6 and the sand dune 3.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Litter pieces before and after. Before 10 pieces, After 0 pieces.
figures.caption: Litter pieces before the clean-up: 10. After: 0.
